articles.title: New Python packages picked hatchling, not uv_build
articles.excerpt: On Monday, Michał Górny from Gentoo posted a plea not to use uv-build. It's a Rust backend with 1.2-1.5 MiB wheels and a dozen releases a month, and Gentoo users have to build every one of them from s…
articles.body: On Monday, Michał Górny from Gentoo posted a plea not to use uv-build . It's a Rust backend with 1.2-1.5 MiB wheels and a dozen releases a month, and Gentoo users have to build every one of them from source, all so it can zip up some pure Python files. Fair enough really. But it made me wonder how many people acutally use it. uv is everywhere now, and since uv 0.8 in July 2025, uv init --package hands you uv_build out of the box. So surely that's what new packages are built with? Nope. About one in twenty. Here's what new PyPI projects have been using each month: Build backend of new PyPI projects ( the data ) Share of each month's sample of new projects, read from the first source release they uploaded The one that moved is hatchling.

articles.title: How to add an embedded wallet to a React app (Google login, gasless transactions)
articles.excerpt: Most people who bounce off a web3 app never get past the "install a browser extension and write down 24 words" step. An embedded wallet removes that step: the user signs in with Google, gets an addres…
articles.body: Most people who bounce off a web3 app never get past the "install a browser extension and write down 24 words" step. An embedded wallet removes that step: the user signs in with Google, gets an address, and can send a transaction without ever holding gas. This post walks through wiring that up in a React app with @cavos/kit , an embedded wallet SDK that supports Starknet, Solana and Stellar. I'll use Starknet for the main example because it shows the most moving parts (a paymaster, a multicall, lazy deployment), and point out where Solana and Stellar differ.

articles.title: Work Architecture and Automation: Productivity and Meaning
articles.excerpt: The article analyzes the transformation of the labor market under the influence of generative AI, rejecting the simplified vision of professions disappearing entirely. The author emphasizes that a pro…
articles.body: The article analyzes the transformation of the labor market under the influence of generative AI, rejecting the simplified vision of professions disappearing entirely. The author emphasizes that a profession is a package of heterogeneous tasks, only some of which are subject to automation. Using the Acemoglu and Restrepo model, the text explains the dynamics between the displacement effect and the reinstatement effect (the creation of new roles). The key conclusion is that the impact of technology is not merely an economic issue but concerns the foundations of social architecture: identity, status, and the feeling of being needed.

articles.title: Windsurf vs Cursor vs Cline: how I'd actually pick one in 2026
articles.excerpt: The autocomplete era is over. Nobody serious is still writing functions off ghost-text suggestions. The real question in 2026 isn't "should I use an AI coding tool," it's "which agent do I hand the ke…
articles.body: The autocomplete era is over. Nobody serious is still writing functions off ghost-text suggestions. The real question in 2026 isn't "should I use an AI coding tool," it's "which agent do I hand the keys to." And honestly, Windsurf, Cursor, and Cline are built for three genuinely different kinds of developer. Here's how I'd choose, minus the marketing. Pick Cursor if you want "it just works" Cursor is the safe default, and I mean that as a compliment. It's a VS Code fork, so there's no new environment to learn, your extensions and keybinds come along, and the whole thing is fast and polished. Its real strength is the multi-file refactor (Composer). Point it at a change that spans a dozen files and it handles the plumbing without going rogue.

articles.title: Merged Is Not Shipped. The Fix Has to Exist in the Tree That Runs.
articles.excerpt: At 1:36 in the morning, a fix my team had built was merged into our main branch. Nineteen minutes later, the scheduled job it was built to rescue ran — and failed in exactly the old way, because the j…
articles.body: At 1:36 in the morning, a fix my team had built was merged into our main branch. Nineteen minutes later, the scheduled job it was built to rescue ran — and failed in exactly the old way, because the job does not run from main. It runs from a different checkout, and nobody had put the fix there. Merged is a state of a repository. Shipped is a state of the machine that does the work. Confusing the two is how "fixed" bugs survive the night. The fix itself was good. One of our production services depends on a token that expires on a schedule, and a patrol job refreshes it and pushes the new value to production. That push kept dying against a platform upload quota — not a code error, a rationing wall: too many file uploads in the window, try again tomorrow.

articles.title: Track job applications from Gmail automatically with n8n and AI
articles.excerpt: After the twentieth job application, nobody remembers which company replied, which one sent a coding test with a Friday deadline, and which one quietly rejected you three weeks ago. The usual advice i…
articles.body: After the twentieth job application, nobody remembers which company replied, which one sent a coding test with a Friday deadline, and which one quietly rejected you three weeks ago. The usual advice is "keep a spreadsheet". The problem is that keeping the spreadsheet is a second job. But almost every update in a job search already arrives as an email: the "thanks for applying" confirmation, the assessment link, the interview invite, the rejection. So the spreadsheet can maintain itself. This post walks through an n8n workflow that watches Gmail, uses Google Gemini (free tier) to recognise emails about your applications, and keeps one row per application in Google Sheets with the latest status, next step and deadline.

articles.title: 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds
articles.excerpt: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of dark matter, the mysterious stuff that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.
articles.body: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds. For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter , whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe . Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

articles.body: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23). The mission lifted off aboard an Electron rocket from Rocket Lab’s New Zealand launch site today at 3:11 a.m. EDT (0711 GMT; 8:11 p.m. local time in New Zealand). The Electron carried three "Hawk" satellites for the Virginia-based company HawkEye 360, which explains the name Rocket Lab gave to the mission: "We're Not Hawking Around." If all goes according to plan, the three Hawks will be deployed into low Earth orbit (LEO), at an altitude of 323 miles (520 kilometers). Once up there and commissioned, the satellites will scan the globe for radio frequency (RF) emissions.

articles.title: Space debris: Are we on track for true sustainability? (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: Space is a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. It’s therefore critical to maintain a safe and clean orbital environment.
articles.body: David Zamora is the chairman of the Space Data Association. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The commercialization of space is well underway, and as a result, Earth’s orbit is becoming ever more congested. The current number of active satellites in orbit stands at around 16,000, according to the European Space Agency( ESA), and this number is expected to jump close to 60,000 by 2035, Novaspace projects . While it’s not always given the recognition it deserves, space has fast become a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. Therefore, it’s critical that a safe and clean operating landscape is maintained.

articles.title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
articles.excerpt: The full-scale prototype of Europe's Space Rider orbiter failed to deploy its parachute during a drop test earlier this month, but ESA officials hope the setback won't delay progress toward its first…
articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.body: Canva is diving even deeper into AI with the launch of an image generation model that competes directly with those from OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. The model, called Canva Craft , uses a two-stage architecture that allows it to plan a design before generating an image, allowing for "greater precision, consistency and control," according to an announcement on Thursday . Canva Craft can generate images at up to 2K resolution and in more than 30 aspect ratios. In addition to generating social media posts and marketing content, it's also supposed to create realistic scenes, digital art, environmental imagery, and more. articles.title: NASA Invites Media to 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium
articles.excerpt: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s sym…
articles.body: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s symposium is focused on humanity’s return to the Moon, sustainable lunar infrastructure, advanced space propulsion, and the evolving space workforce. Panels include discussions on Artemis II and III, space propulsion flash talks, building utilities and infrastructure for sustainable lunar operations, Moon base supply chain resilience, space nuclear technology, navigating the new NASA workforce, and engineering the future, featuring keynotes and awards presentations.
